clue.text: Silent old film

parts.note: dumb is an old word for unable to speak, so silent

explanation.surface: A reference to a silent movie from the early days of cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent old film' reads as one phrase describing a picture from before the talkies, but only 'film' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1941 animated feature about a flying baby elephant carries this title.

clue.text: Decline to make a move, of course

explanation.surface: Refusing to take a step, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means on a golf course, where this is part of the swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or downturn in trade; and in golf, the club's descending stroke towards the ball.

clue.text: Stateswomen perhaps crammed in ladies uncomfortably

indicators.note: being packed uncomfortably suggests the letters jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: Women from various US states squeezed awkwardly into a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stateswomen' looks like female politicians, but means women of the States (the USA).
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary, conservative citizens of the American heartland include women from those States.

clue.text: Business organisation given hospital work

explanation.surface: A company takes on medical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or enterprise running a business; and surgery performed on a patient by a surgeon.

clue.text: First class social function

explanation.surface: A top-quality party or gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools the youngest class, which children join at four or five, is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the starting class of an English primary school, and a formal party such as a wedding celebration.

clue.text: He owned cinemas where Taxi Driver could be seen

definitions.text: where Taxi Driver could be seen

explanation.surface: A cinema chain owner screened the film Taxi Driver.
explanation.walkthrough: J Arthur Rank ran the Odeon cinema chain in Britain. 'Taxi Driver' looks like the Scorsese film, but is just a cabbie waiting at a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: J Arthur Rank was the British film magnate; and a cab stand is where cabbies queue for fares.

clue.text: Take a moment in resort? That's not very long

indicators.note: in means the one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a centre is a place people resort to, as a holiday or leisure centre
time means a particular moment

explanation.surface: Advice to pause briefly while on holiday, since the stay is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not very long' sounds like a remark on time, but describes a tiny length.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a metre is a very short measure of length.

clue.text: Turning up late after start of performance is a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the other one
the start of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: Arriving late to a show is something of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses LATE to ETAL. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that blooms, and one segment of its corolla is a small piece of it.

clue.text: A question Lenin resolved about origin of Communism being of no significance

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses another
resolved here means broken up and worked out again, so the letters are rearranged
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lenin settled a question about the roots of Communism, which proved unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' makes INONSEQUENTIAL from the letters, and 'about' wraps them round the C. 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial or unimportant matters not at all.

clue.text: Low point said to be not so sweet

indicators.note: said to be signals that the letters are a word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: nay is an old word for no or not; dear means sweet or lovable

explanation.surface: Someone's worst moment is reckoned to be less sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, the opposite of the zenith, figuratively the worst moment.

clue.text: Remove end from device attached to bird

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for the device is cut off

parts.note: a widget is a small gadget or device
on means attached, as a light that is on is connected

explanation.surface: An instruction to detach part of a gadget fixed to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove end from' takes the T off WIDGET, leaving WIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of dabbling duck, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Less sickly way of presenting cake, it's remarked

definitions.text: Less sickly way of presenting cake

explanation.surface: A remark that a cake is less cloying served plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ICED, the first part describes a cake without its sugary topping, which is less sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake without frosting is less sickly; and to have observed or commented on something is to have spotted it.

clue.text: Polite greeting unfortunately rejected by American

indicators.note: rejected suggests something thrown back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A courteous greeting is sadly rebuffed by someone from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sounds like the greeting being rebuffed, but it reverses the word for 'unfortunately'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a low bow with the hand on the forehead, a respectful salutation in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Hat maker works in outskirts of Exeter

parts.note: a mill is a factory or works

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone who makes hats is employed on the edge of a Devon city.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who designs and sells women's headwear is a hatter by trade.

clue.text: As it were, terribly hot inside a launderette

indicators.note: inside means the one letter goes within the anagrammed letters
terribly signals the letters are scrambled badly

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A launderette became awfully hot inside, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges AS IT WERE as WASETERI, and 'inside' puts H within it, after WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned name for a self-service laundry.

clue.text: Thing that's still popular with a friend from Ulster, mind

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
NI is Northern Ireland, which is often called Ulster
mate is an informal word for a friend
to mind something is to object to it

explanation.surface: Something motionless pleases a pal from Northern Ireland, though they may disapprove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is an adjective here (motionless), not an adverb meaning 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock or chair is a lifeless article that never moves of its own accord.

clue.text: Singers I note performing in parts of pub

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a pub has several bars, such as the public and saloon bars

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters acting out a new routine, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Vocalists sing a note as they perform in various rooms of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' is the anagram signal on the musical word. A British pub traditionally has several rooms, such as the public and saloon, which supply the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Male voices pitched between tenor and bass belong to these singers.

clue.text: Right to look into master spy's ultimate act of betrayal

indicators.note: to look into something is to go inside it

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spymaster's final betrayal is being investigated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master spy' reads as a spymaster, but 'master' is TEACHER and 'spy's ultimate' is Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason or disloyalty is the act of betraying trust.

clue.text: Eco-warrior introduces plan to recycle? That's the spirit

parts.note: a green is an environmental campaigner
a chart is a plan or map
to reuse something is to recycle it

explanation.surface: An environmental activist presents a recycling scheme, and someone cheers it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the spirit' sounds like encouragement, but it points to an alcoholic spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so a type of spirit.

clue.text: Foreigner mostly absorbs language used in Spanish resort

indicators.note: absorbs means takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner
cant is jargon, the language of a particular group

explanation.surface: A tourist picks up the local lingo on a Spanish holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ALIEN to ALIE, which 'absorbs' CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city on Spain's Costa Blanca is a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Film director offers a small part to actor named Harris

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for part
Ed Harris is an American film actor

explanation.surface: A director offers a minor role to an actor called Harris.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Apted is the British director of the Up series of documentaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Apted directed Coal Miner's Daughter and a Bond film.

clue.text: Put out a request, wanting a stamp

indicators.note: put out means expelled, so that letter is removed

parts.note: an appeal is an earnest request

explanation.surface: Someone issues a plea because they need a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamp' is not postage but a fencing move: a stamp of the front foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing, a sharp beat of the leading foot on the floor is a feint signal.

clue.text: A medicinal preparation to make all you stress-free

parts.note: a tonic is a medicine taken to invigorate

explanation.surface: A remedy that promises to calm everybody down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress-free' means unstressed in the phonetic sense, as a syllable with no accent, not relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a syllable without accent is described by this term.

clue.text: Talented old movie star needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A famous gifted actor of old who needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' sounds like praise for fame, but removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful and competent means gifted at something.

clue.text: One walks wearily, going round fabric shop in America

indicators.note: going round suggests turning back on itself, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used in upholstery
mart is a US word for a store

explanation.surface: Someone trudges tiredly around a US textile store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns REPMART into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tramps is a hiker who trudges heavily on foot.

clue.text: German engineer in the east discovered petrol product

parts.note: Karl Benz was the German engineer who built an early motor car
E is the standard abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A German engineer working in the east finds a new fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: BENZ is Karl Benz, of Mercedes-Benz fame.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a volatile liquid distilled from petroleum, used as a solvent and fuel.

clue.text: Place in grip of sickness bug

indicators.note: held in the grip of something means placed inside it

parts.note: disease means sickness
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Somewhere gripped by an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' is a verb here, meaning annoy, not an insect or germ.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or irritate someone is to upset them.

clue.text: Vehicle for transporting one is withdrawn

explanation.surface: A one-person vehicle is taken off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A sulky is a light two-wheeled cart for a single driver, used in harness racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A light one-seat horse cart used in trotting races; and moody, sullen and uncommunicative.
